items.name: Added by the user 2026-11-10 [opus]: turn the loop status board into a live flow view with a chat to the orchestrator. Inspiration images (read only, look at both): `<scratch>/2.png` (node flow: stages, parallel branches, feedback arrow, billing band) and `...\images\4.png` (agent tree: nodes with state, effort bars, spawned workers, session log). Take the way the data flows, not the look; keep the board's current dark style. Branch `feat/board-flow` from `main`, own PR against `main`, never merge. Build on `skills/agent-work-modes/scripts/loop-status.html` and `loop-status.py`. (1) Flow: one node per LOOP-STATE item laid out by Depends (parallel branches side by side, edges drawn), node states done, running now, todo, waiting for a dependency, BLOCKED waits for the user, each with a visible badge and what it waits on; a node for the driver and the live `claude -p` round with its subagents; a feedback arrow when an item retries. (2) Progress: bars for items done of total, rounds used of cap, tries per item, tokens and cost of the run from the usage data. (3) Click a node: side panel with what it does, depends, VERIFY and its evidence from LOOP-HISTORY. (4) Session log: timestamped stream of rounds, commits and usage lines. (5) Chat: a panel where the user writes to the orchestrator; every message carries references picked in the browser (clicked node, selected text, page section). The server appends each message as one JSON line to `orchestrator-inbox.jsonl` in the loop folder (POST `/chat`) and shows replies from `orchestrator-outbox.jsonl` (the orchestrator session watches the inbox with Monitor and answers by appending to the outbox). Keep it free of external requests, English only, works at phone width. VERIFY: headless Chrome screenshots at 1400 and 400 px show flow, bars, log and chat with no console errors; the node count equals the LOOP-STATE row count; a POST to `/chat` with a node reference writes the expected line to the inbox and a line appended to the outbox appears in the page; `python -m pytest skills/agent-work-modes/scripts -q` passes

ev.title: benchmark runs (FAILED, wrong model on 4 of 7 runs)
ev.body:
Ran `bench/run.py` (new) for all 7 forms, 1 run each, all 7 passed the check. Measured with session-cost.py (raw: `bench/usage.json`, `bench/results.jsonl`):

| form | session(s) | model actually used | US$ | ctx start>peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| conversation | b5a02918 | sonnet-5-5 | 0.18 | 38k>40k |
| goal | c8469a46 | **opus-5-5** | 0.36 | 36k>40k |
| stophook | 70edf771 | sonnet-5-5 | 0.12 | 38k>40k |
| subagents | 51c5d783 | **opus-5-5** | 0.23 | 36k>40k |
| workflow | a5d11cd4 | **opus-5-5** | 0.23 | 36k>40k |
| loop | 3bc35b81 | **opus-5-5** | 0.24 | 36k>40k |
| fresh | 01bed476 +2 | sonnet-5-5 | 0.10 (3 sessions) | 13k>15k |

Problem: every `claude -p` call passed `--model sonnet`, yet goal/subagents/workflow/loop ran on opus (cause not found; the prompt was passed through cmd.exe quoting, suspect). This breaks the fixed-model rule of the protocol and the user's no-opus order (about US$1.06 of API-price estimate on opus). Results are NOT comparable and must not feed item 20. Not rerun this round. Next try: pass the prompt via stdin, verify the model in the first session before the rest, and rerun only the 4 affected forms.
